propositions: Core push delivery performs exactly five retry cycles with fetch-merge recovery only after retriable non-fast-forward rejection, followed by one conditional terminal push that executes only if the fifth rejection produces a clean merged HEAD.
Opt-in strict delivery raises a catchable PushDeliveryError with stable machine-readable reasons and unpushed-commit count, while best-effort (default) remains unchanged for all existing callers.
All pre-existing library, CLI, MCP, importer, and store-write callers retain their legacy best-effort disposition by omitting strict or reaching the core with strict=False.

The private Python adapter process boundary (python -m rebar._store.push push --strict) translates PushDeliveryError to stderr and nonzero exit without calling sys.exit or writing ticket events or BRIDGE_ALERT files.
Dirty-tree staging and committing remain outside push_tickets_branch; the retry-budget and terminal-push logic apply only to the delivery phase.
